assessments.reasoning: The W3C Recommendation and its exact digest are authentic. §2.10 establishes the pass-through rule for non-markup characters and a separate whitespace-reporting obligation for validating processors. The frozen claim applies broadly to any processor and states normalization as its scope qualifier. §§4.4.3 and 5.1 also permit a non-validating processor to omit a referenced external parsed entity's replacement text, with notification to the application. The candidate does not limit the domain to characters read and included under those rules.

challenge.method: Compare §2.10 to the markup definition and the external-entity inclusion rules. Challenge the claim with a non-validating processor that recognizes a reference but does not read the external replacement text, and with whitespace outside the document element.
challenge.results: The clause supports a pass-through obligation for eligible included input and does not transfer top-level whitespace defined as markup. An allowed skipped entity is a material limitation on any document-wide reading. The broadly scoped frozen revision leaves that boundary unresolved.

limitations: A narrower statement should expressly describe the scope of the §2.10 obligation under the entity inclusion rules. The separate validating-processor obligation remains supported.
